question: Where does the baby's occiput point in an occipito-posterior position?
explanation: In an occipito-posterior position, the back of the baby's head is directed backward toward the mother's spine, which is why it is called posterior. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do babies in an occipito-posterior position often cause longer labors?

options.A: They enter the pelvis with a wider head diameter due to less flexion
options.B: They prefer to sleep longer inside the uterus during contractions
options.C: They automatically cause the cervix to close up tighter during labor
options.D: They completely block the flow of amniotic fluid early in pregnancy

explanation: When the fetal head is less tucked or deflexed, a larger diameter of the skull presents to the pelvis, making descent slower and more difficult. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which pelvic shape is most commonly associated with an occipito-posterior position?
explanation: The android pelvis has a narrow front shape that encourages the baby's head to turn toward the wider back part of the pelvis. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h2)

question: How do weak abdominal muscles contribute to an occipito-posterior position?

options.A: They make the pelvic bones softer and wider than normal
options.B: They stop the mother from feeling any contractions at all
options.C: They block the baby's heart rate from accelerating during contractions
options.D: They fail to press the baby firmly against the front wall of the uterus

explanation: Good abdominal muscle tone helps keep the baby flexed and positioned against the front of the belly, whereas lower tone lets the baby settle backward. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h2)

question: Where are fetal heart sounds typically auscultated when the baby is in an OP position?

options.A: High up near the top of the fundus
options.B: Far out toward the mother's flank
options.C: Directly in the center of the umbilicus
options.D: Directly over the mother's pubic bone

explanation: Because the baby's chest and back are turned toward the mother's back, the heart sounds travel outward and are best heard far to the side. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h3)

question: A laboring woman complains of severe, constant lower backache and feels her baby's kicking limbs all over the front of her belly. What position is most likely?
explanation: Feeling limbs across the front and experiencing intense back pain are classic signs that the baby's head is pressing backward against the sacrum. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h3)

question: How many degrees must the occiput rotate forward for a normal vaginal delivery from an OP position?
explanation: The baby has to travel a longer distance, rotating 135 degrees forward to bring the occiput under the pubic symphysis. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h4)

question: What happens when an OP baby fails to complete its long internal rotation inside the pelvis?
explanation: If the head stops turning and gets stuck sideways in the mid-pelvis, it is known as a deep transverse arrest requiring professional intervention. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication of a persistent occipito-posterior position?

options.A: Rapid painless labor within one hour

explanation: OP labor is typically very slow, painful, and prolonged rather than fast and painless. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why does a baby in an OP position often develop swelling (caput succedaneum) on the head?

options.A: Too much oxygen entering the fetal brain during contractions
options.B: An infection caught inside the amniotic fluid before labor begins
options.C: Prolonged pressure from the cervix against the tightly fitted pelvic bones
options.D: A genetic condition affecting how skin grows on the scalp

explanation: The tight fit and prolonged labor put constant pressure on the baby's scalp, causing fluid to collect under the skin. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why are hands-and-knees or leaning forward positions recommended for an OP labor?

options.A: They force the cervix to dilate by three centimeters instantly
options.B: Gravity helps the heavy fetal spine swing forward toward the front
options.C: They prevent the baby from moving at all during the second stage
options.D: They completely stop the mother from feeling any contractions

explanation: Postures that lean the mother forward shift the weight of the baby's back, encouraging the head to rotate into a more favorable position. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h6)

question: A midwife is caring for a woman with an OP position who is exhausted from severe back pain during contractions. What is the best immediate non-pharmacological nursing action?

options.A: Restrict all oral fluids until the baby is fully born
options.B: Apply counter-pressure and lower back massage during contractions
options.C: Tell the woman to push hard before the cervix is fully dilated
options.D: Instruct the woman to lie flat on her back with legs tightly closed

explanation: Counter-pressure and massage provide relief for the intense sacral back pain associated with posterior positions. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h6)
